m1-repo-revision-fn.title: checklist_engine.repo_revision(): commit + dirty, computed once, off context_manifest.py's own AST-banned-subprocess surface
m1-repo-revision-fn.imperative: Add a `repo_revision(base_dir) -> {'commit': str|None, 'dirty': bool|None}` function to scripts/checklist_engine.py, reusing the existing `_git()` subprocess helper (already used for git-change-policy) -- `git rev-parse HEAD` for commit, `git status --porcelain` for dirty, both scoped to base_dir. Any git failure (not a repo, git missing) yields {'commit': None, 'dirty': None}, never raises -- mirrors the existing 'absence is normal, never raise' rule read_bytes()/rev() already follow for file rows. This function must live in checklist_engine.py, NOT context_manifest.py: tests/test_context_manifest.py::ProducerGuards::test_producer_shells_out_to_nothing AST-scans context_manifest.py's own source for subprocess/socket/etc identifiers and must keep passing untouched. Add tests to tests/test_checklist_engine.py asserting: commit matches `git rev-parse HEAD` oracle on this real repo; dirty is a bool computed from `git status --porcelain` non-emptiness (oracle-compared); a non-git directory (tempdir) yields {'commit': None, 'dirty': None} without raising. Test-after is fine (this is a thin subprocess wrapper mirroring the existing `_collect_changed_files` pattern, not a novel algorithm). Attest c1 (TDD not required here) and satisfy c2 (command).

postconditions.statement: test-after acceptable here; no TDD red step required -- thin wrapper over the existing _git() subprocess helper
repo_revision() present, tested, graceful on non-git dirs; full checklist_engine suite still green

m2-manifest-content-field.title: repo_rev admitted into CONTENT_KEYS, wired via a second injectable impure edge
m2-manifest-content-field.imperative: In scripts/context_manifest.py: add `default_repo_state(roots) -> dict` (a pure-looking wrapper that calls `checklist_engine.repo_revision(roots.get('repo'))`, imported by name -- never `import subprocess`, so the module's own AST-banned-identifier guard stays clean), add a `repo_state` parameter to `build_manifest` defaulting to `default_repo_state`, add `'repo_rev'` to `CONTENT_KEYS` (before `run`, so the envelope stays CONTENT_KEYS + {run}), and emit `'repo_rev': dict(repo_state(roots))` in the manifest between `files` and `run`. Update the module docstring's 'single impure edge' claim to 'two impure edges' (reader for file bytes, repo_state for repo-level commit/dirty) and its point-1 paragraph to mention the new field briefly. Do NOT touch `rev()` or the per-file row shape -- the per-file blob OID stays byte-for-byte what it is. Update the one pre-existing test that hardcodes the 4-key envelope (`ManifestEnvelope.test_envelope_has_exactly_four_keys` -> 5 keys, in the new order) since it must legitimately change; every other pre-existing test should keep passing because they assert via `set(...)`/`CONTENT_KEYS`, not a hardcoded list. Add a new test class in tests/test_context_manifest.py (method names containing 'repo_rev', matching gate g5's `-k 'repo_rev or doctrine_version'` selector) covering: repo_rev is in CONTENT_KEYS; repo_rev survives into content(); repo_rev shape is exactly {commit, dirty}; repo_state is injectable (fake callable's return flows through untouched, mirroring the existing reader-injection test); default_repo_state against the real repo matches the `git rev-parse HEAD` / `git status --porcelain` oracles (test file only -- subprocess-as-oracle is fine there, unlike in the producer itself). Attest c1 (test-after, inspection-mode: this is wiring an existing tested primitive into an existing tested envelope, not new algorithmic risk) and satisfy c2/c3 (commands).

m3-determinism-check.title: The critical check: cross-environment determinism test passes UNCHANGED
m3-determinism-check.imperative: Run tests/test_context_determinism.py against the now-edited scripts/context_manifest.py and scripts/checklist_engine.py WITHOUT modifying that test file at all. It builds two fresh git worktrees at the SAME commit, overlays the current (in-progress) copies of context_manifest.py/checklist_engine.py onto both, and asserts the content projection (now including repo_rev) is byte-identical across both environments. If it passes: attest c1 and move on -- this is confirmation, not new work. If it FAILS: STOP. Do not patch the test, do not move the field into `run`, do not add masking. Report the failure as a design-invalidating finding in IMPLEMENTER_RESULT's stop conditions section instead -- per the dispatch instructions this would mean the field belongs in the excluded /run subtree after all, which is a bigger finding than this gate's budget covers.
